thread:
incident-bot: Pager: high-severity alerts - multiple tokenizer pods OOM in us-west-2-runtime cluster, start time ~1901234567.

Lee Chen: acked - coming in now. any clue which deployment?

Jordan Park: seeing lots of pod evictions on tokenizer-worker-{0..4}, CPU usage pinned at 100% for >2m then kernel OOM kills.

Maya Singh: confirmed, logs show repeated `Killed process` entries. stack traces indicate tokenizer subprocess looping on large prompt batches.

Jordan Park: sample log:```
Mar 04 14:22:11 host kubelet: Container failed liveness probe: read tcp 10.0.2.5:443: connection reset by peer
Mar 04 14:22:13 host kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (tokenizer) total-vm:123456kB, anon-rss:110000kB, file-rss:2000kB
Mar 04 14:22:13 host kubelet: Pod "tokenizer-worker-2" evicted due to node OOM
```

Lee Chen: paging oncall-sre. Jordan/Maya you two take triage, I'll be incident lead unless someone objects.

Priya Nair: I'm next oncall in 30m, happy to take handoff if this is ongoing.

Jordan Park: quick assessment: spike correlates with a single customer sending huge batch prompts that hit server-side batching. We have no per-request token limit on the tokenize stage so CPU climbs and threads spawn.

Maya Singh: customer ID 9243 shows ~2k requests/minute with 50k token prompts. that's abnormal.

DevOps Bot: Automated mitigation suggestion: scale tokenizer deployment to 8 replicas, set resource limits to 1.5 CPU, and set env TOKENIZER_MAX_THREADS=2 via rollout. Would you like me to apply? :robot_face:

Lee Chen: do it. also add a temporary IncomingRateLimiter at the ingress to throttle that customer IP to 10 rps.

Jordan Park: running commands now:
```bash
kubectl set env deploy/tokenizer-worker TOKENIZER_MAX_THREADS=2 -n runtime
kubectl patch deploy/tokenizer-worker -n runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"tokenizer","resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"1500m"},"requests":{"cpu":"500m"}}}]}}}}'
kubectl scale deploy/tokenizer-worker --replicas=8 -n runtime
```

Maya Singh: ingress rule added to rate-limit via kong: `limit_by_ip: 10 rps` for customer 9243. Also temporarily disabled batch-merge preprocessor (flag: PREPROC_BATCHING=false).

DevOps Bot: Patch applied and scaled. New pods are coming up.

Jordan Park: new pods healthy but we still see a small wave of evictions on two old nodes. cordoning node ip-10-0-3-21 and draining to avoid further evictions.

Lee Chen: cordon/drain in progress. Also rolling restart of affected tokenizer pods to clear any leaked state.

Maya Singh: customer impact: ~8% of hosted inference requests returned 5xx during window 14:22-14:35 UTC. Affected tenants: 3 customers (IDs: 9243, 1182, 3010). 9243 accounts for ~70% of error volume.

Priya Nair: putting together status for CS: short blurb: "Tokenization service hit CPU OOM due to unusually large batched prompts from a single customer; we throttled the customer, applied resource limits, scaled replicas, and disabled batching. Services are recovering; some 5xx errors occurred during 14:22-14:35 UTC. Follow-up: enforce max token/per-request at gateway and add per-customer throttles."

Lee Chen: Jordan - can you fallback heavy requests to smaller tokenizer variant or queue them?

Jordan Park: pushed a temporary fallback policy: requests over 10k tokens now route to tokenizer-lite model with lower memory profile. config change applied via configstore.

Maya Singh: watch: CPU has dropped to ~45% across new pods. evictions stopped.

DevOps Bot: incident severity set to SEV2, ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4921

Lee Chen: good. handoff to Priya in 25m. Priya, I'll leave the summary+open actions in the ticket.

Priya Nair: taking over. current ACTIONS: 1) enforce gateway token limit 2) add per-customer qps guardrails 3) add tokenizer per-request token cap and hard-kill long-running tokenizers after 30s 4) postmortem owner: Jordan Park.

Jordan Park: will own postmortem. initial blameless notes: missing upstream request size checks and no per-customer throttling.

Maya Singh: notifying affected customers via CS now, include incident ticket link and mitigation steps.

Lee Chen: nice work. one follow-up: add telemetry to batch sizes and tokenizer thread counts so we can alert before OOM.

Priya Nair: noted, I'll add alerting playbook and create a dashboard for batch sizes.

Lee Chen: handing off fully to Priya at 14:50 UTC. final note: if we still see evictions after 15:00 UTC, escalate to infra with node-level analysis.

Priya Nair: ack, taking ownership. closing slack thread when stable. :white_check_mark:
